newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria lifts ban on airline grounded after crash.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria lifts ban on airline grounded after crash.

text.p: A Nigerian airline grounded after one of its planes crashed three weeks ago killing all 142 people on board can now resume operations again, local newspapers reported on Saturday.
Aviation minister Air Commodore Ita Udo-Imeh lifted the ban when he visited the offices of Aviation Development Company (ADC) in the capital Abuja on Friday, the newspapers said.

"Having carried out the additional thorough and painstaking checks on all aspects of ADC's fleet and found the planes to be in satisfactory condition, we are satisfied that the airline is fit to resume the normal business of flying," Udo-Imeh said.
ADC, which has seven aircraft, was grounded two weeks after its Boeing 727 plane flying from the southeastern oil city of Port Harcourt crashed into a lagoon northeast of Lagos on November 7.
The bodies have yet to be recovered.
The crash, the worst in Nigeria since 1992 when a C-130 transport plane went down in swamps near Lagos killing 173 people, caused much anxiety among the travelling public.

The share price of ADC, owned by a group of Nigerian pilots and the only airline to be quoted on the stock exchange, fell sharply after the crash and was suspended from trading by the exchange authorities last Wednesday.
ADC's spokesman Utibe Ukim welcomed the government reprieve, saying efforts would be made to resume flying soon.
"The grounding of our operations necessitated the shutdown of our system including the decision to ask all our staff to proceed on leave," he told Thisday newspaper.
